dimensions.reachable_storage: Eight inline child records plus actual pthread stacks; nested tree adds two groups and four retained task contexts. Live stack attributes are virtual reservations, not resident pages.
dimensions.lifetime: Start admission precedes task entry; cancel records intent; every admitted child must join before its context can be released. A descendant still running retains every enclosing owner.
dimensions.mutation_aliasing: One owner mutates nursery admission/join records. Children read atomic cancellation and publish context results before join synchronization; arbitrary parallel spawn is not admitted.
dimensions.allocation: Nursery metadata is caller-owned; pthread_create can allocate internally and fail. All eight injected admission positions preserve earlier children for joining.
dimensions.movement_copying: No whole nursery copy is a move: child owner pointers retain the original address. Task contexts remain borrowed at fixed addresses until the matching join.
dimensions.destruction: At most eight joins in a flat nursery, but no finite latency without cooperative child termination and scheduling assumptions. Nested teardown joins leaves before parents.
dimensions.dispatch: Task entry and destructor callbacks are indirect; mfn_pool_task invokes the actual earlier hosted pool. The timing workload measures simple cooperative children separately.
dimensions.concurrency: Atomic cancel publication does not establish child completion. Creation-order error choice remains deterministic under reversed completion schedules; both failures survive the bounded aggregate.
dimensions.failure: Admission failure triggers cancellation and retains prior admissions. Ninth/late admission refuses; empty join succeeds; attempt exhaustion refuses before thread creation.
dimensions.boundary: POSIX thread creation/join and GNU live-stack query are host contracts. Neither ISO C nor a stack size query supplies a real-time or maximum-used-stack guarantee.

dimensions.reachable_storage: Two queues of up to four copied values; owning successor adds eight stable message records. Registered select adds one caller-stack node per live select and two channel locks plus registry.
dimensions.lifetime: Enqueued ownership survives sender return; rendezvous acceptance differs from an outstanding offer. Registration nodes remain linked through predicate wait and are removed before return.
dimensions.mutation_aliasing: Common-hub mutex protects the original predicates; split design uses channel-before-registry order. Concurrent selectors may consume a wakeup candidate before another selector resumes.
dimensions.allocation: Queue and ownership metadata are inline. The observer sample arrays and producer payload allocation are host-test costs; original unsigned timing has no payload allocation.
dimensions.movement_copying: Unsigned values are copied; owning descriptors transfer only on accepted send. Receiver extraction does not deep-copy payload storage. Failed publication retains the sender owner.
dimensions.destruction: Destruction drains accepted owners only after admission closes and active calls quiesce. Callback runtime is not bounded by the eight metadata slots.
dimensions.dispatch: Common select scans two channels; registration scans two channels and notifies O(W) active waiter nodes. Mutex and condition operations cross the POSIX library boundary.
dimensions.concurrency: Sticky notification plus registration-before-scan closes the empty-observation/sleep window. Signals require predicate recheck; pthread cancellation unwinding is explicitly not supported.
dimensions.failure: FULL/EMPTY preserve output/owner; close drains accepted values; cancel distinguishes accepted from unaccepted rendezvous. BUSY destruction retains the object until calls finish.
dimensions.boundary: Deterministic rotating selection is not Go randomized selection. Coroutine ticket import retains frames through external worker join and explicit acknowledgement; tokens alone do not prove quiescence.

dimensions.reachable_storage: Serialized operation is inline; concurrent successor allocates one independent control with atomic flags/count and retains it for all contenders, separately from receiver-owned application context.
dimensions.lifetime: Connect/start grants one terminal delivery. Inline receiver may free the application object; concurrent losers retain only their control and must never access the freed receiver context.
dimensions.mutation_aliasing: Serialized original requires caller exclusion. Concurrent successor admits one atomic completion winner before ordinary operation/pending fields; each thread owns a separately retained token.
dimensions.allocation: Inline adapter allocates nothing. Concurrent control allocation can fail without publishing output; retain is allocation-free and refuses SIZE_MAX count.
dimensions.movement_copying: Completion clears the unique descriptor before receiver invocation. A descriptor move is not a payload clone; failed/losing completion preserves the contender owner.
dimensions.destruction: One terminal payload release and one final control free; receiver/destructor latency is externally supplied. Stop request neither destroys control nor joins backend work.
dimensions.dispatch: Backend and receiver are indirect calls. Observed GCC O3 mfo_start caches backend/context before calling; msg_complete stores DONE before the callback and has no subsequent object load.
dimensions.concurrency: Cancellation and completion claim share an atomic modification order in the concurrent successor. Earlier cancellation fixes the stopped result; late cancellation cannot revise the winner.
dimensions.failure: Invalid status/descriptor rejects. Duplicate claim returns BUSY. Cancellation before completion produces no early receiver; receiver-free tests and retained losers distinguish lifetime from arbitration.
dimensions.boundary: Dated P2300 comparison does not confer C++ lifetime/type enforcement on an exposed C struct. Public token discipline and normal-return callbacks remain caller obligations.

dimensions.reachable_storage: Four queued messages plus one currently executing owned record; executor adds two actual actors and eight envelopes. Externally allocated payload storage is additional reachable memory.
dimensions.lifetime: Executor owns dispatch; handler borrows one payload through return. Submitted generation is immutable in its envelope; restart never retags already accepted work.
dimensions.mutation_aliasing: One executor mutates actor state. Producers publish through the actual owning hub; pool mutex protects stable envelopes. Blocking self-send can deadlock the sole consumer and is prohibited.
dimensions.allocation: Actor/executor metadata is inline; payload allocation belongs to producers. Pool exhaustion and channel refusal preserve caller ownership until acceptance.
dimensions.movement_copying: Channel moves one unique envelope; executor extracts payload and frees the slot before actor dispatch. Self-enqueue moves a separate owner without recursive handler entry.
dimensions.destruction: Failure drops active/queued owners once; stale messages go to a consuming dead-letter sink. Restart and destruction refuse while stepping; callback costs remain external.
dimensions.dispatch: Handler and dead-letter dispatch are indirect. One pump delivers one accepted event. The measured actor cycle excludes allocating payload and cross-thread queue latency.
dimensions.concurrency: The2,000-message threaded test compares the observed actor effect order to a mutex-protected reference, not all possible histories or performance superiority.
dimensions.failure: FULL/CLOSED retain owners before admission; STALE consumes to dead letters. Generation exhaustion retires. Effects emitted by a handler before it fails remain observable.
dimensions.boundary: An incarnation token prevents stale protocol delivery, not forged authority or arbitrary pointer use. C actors provide no process isolation or automatic rollback.

dimensions.reachable_storage: Five supervisor records and16 actual actors in a fixed two-level tree; bounded timestamps and event arrays coexist with externally constructed child resources.
dimensions.lifetime: Stop affected children in reverse dependency order, initialize forward, and close staged resources before escalation. Parent and child budgets are distinct lifetimes.
dimensions.mutation_aliasing: Supervisor calls are serialized and refuse while an actor steps. Constructor/destructor callbacks must not reenter the tree or retain borrowed control storage.
dimensions.allocation: Tree metadata is inline. Fallible resource constructors are explicit; all16 initial failures and partial restart cuts exercise reverse cleanup.
dimensions.movement_copying: Restart plans copy bounded action records. Resource identities are not duplicated by copying actor structs; restart creates a new incarnation after old owned messages are dropped.
dimensions.destruction: Timing replaces two children: two closes/two opens per iteration, plus16 initialization/final operations. Rollback may add callbacks, whose runtime is not bounded by policy.
dimensions.dispatch: Plan generation scans a finite timestamp window and child range; execution dispatches open/close/handler callbacks. A plan is not itself successful recovery.
dimensions.concurrency: A two-level tree is externally serialized; no concurrent supervisor mutation or scheduler independence is claimed. Unlimited recovery requests can amplify failure without intensity limits.
dimensions.failure: Exact expiration boundary admits a fresh restart, backwards time refuses, maximum timestamps are nonwrapping; permanent escalation closes the tree if parent recovery fails.
dimensions.boundary: OTP restart strategy names are comparisons. The C callbacks define actual resource effects; this lab does not inherit Erlang process cleanup or language isolation.

dimensions.reachable_storage: Atomic fixed deque stores eight unsigned slots and nonwrapping indices. Growing pointer successor separately retains allocated arrays and payload controls until all paused thieves release them.
dimensions.lifetime: Owner controls bottom; a successful top compare/exchange transfers one value to a thief. Losing thieves in the pointer variant retain array/payload before dereferencing or racing removal.
dimensions.mutation_aliasing: Only one owner pushes/pops; thieves arbitrate top atomically. Pointer/growth successor uses a mutex for retention and is deliberately not the same lock-free algorithm.
dimensions.allocation: Fixed core allocates nothing. Growth first allocates new array and payload control; each failure preserves old representation. Paused leases can retain old arrays beyond replacement.
dimensions.movement_copying: Unsigned publication copies one value. Growth copies descriptors while retaining node ownership; no copied raw pointer creates an independent lifetime.
dimensions.destruction: Fixed core has no payload destruction. Growing deque releases array/node references, with destruction delayed by paused clients; BUSY teardown preserves active calls.
dimensions.dispatch: Observed GCC O3 weak push uses ordinary mov instructions for release stores; SC push uses xchg. Weak steal retains a locked fence and locked compare/exchange.
dimensions.concurrency: RC11 finite clients validate selected edges and reject omitted-edge controls. Native two/four-thief tests preserve fixed total work; global success does not imply per-thief fairness.
dimensions.failure: EMPTY/FULL/CONFLICT and finite retirement are separate. Failed pop restores bottom. Repeated competing steals can deny one client success despite both taking steps.
dimensions.boundary: Atomic_is_lock_free and emitted x86-64 instructions are host observations. Dynamic reclamation proof does not follow from the fixed-array paper/model and is supplied separately under a mutex.

dimensions.reachable_storage: Four cells with versioned lock words plus bounded read/write sets; owning store adds shared nodes and a64-entry committed synthetic effect log.
dimensions.lifetime: Transaction begins at a clock snapshot; commit locks writes, validates reads, publishes values then unlocks. Dynamic readers retain nodes across replacement/privatization.
dimensions.mutation_aliasing: Payload cells are atomic even for failed transactions. Owning store outer mutex serializes reference acquisition/publication; callbacks cannot publish unlogged external effects safely on retry.
dimensions.allocation: Fixed-cell core allocates nothing. Owning writes stage a new shared node before commit; allocation or log-capacity failure preserves published owners and cleans staged nodes.
dimensions.movement_copying: Read-your-writes reads staged values. Ownership moves into the store only on commit; old nodes are detached and released after the publication lock.
dimensions.destruction: Abort releases staged references and restores acquired version locks. Committed effects publish once; individual release callbacks are outside the mutex and may have external cost.
dimensions.dispatch: Commit visits four bounded cells; retry callback may execute several times. Effect log dispatch occurs only after successful commit, unlike an immediate synthetic side effect.
dimensions.concurrency: SC core provides coherent validated transactions under its fixed-cell proof. Mutex alternative meets the paired-increment contract but differs in refusal/progress. Failed commits may consume clock values.
dimensions.failure: Seven prepublication abort cuts preserve values; nine later observational phases cannot retroactively abort committed data. Invalid read admission preserves the transaction; admitted conflict aborts it.
dimensions.boundary: TL2 algorithm discussion is not a C lifetime proof. Atomic loads do not retain dynamic nodes, and a finite effect log is neither durable storage nor arbitrary effect rollback.

dimensions.reachable_storage: Eight version slots, four pin records; at most five distinct retained versions under four readers. Owned payload leases can outlive both pin and store and add allocated storage.
dimensions.lifetime: Pins retain exact historical visibility; generations validate pin reuse. Shared leases retain payload lifetime separately, including after store destruction.
dimensions.mutation_aliasing: Mutex serializes version selection/publication. Predicate adapter records all observed keys, including zero; write-only validation permits the supplied write-skew counterexample.
dimensions.allocation: Core versions are inline. Owned clone has payload-record, byte-storage and control allocation cuts; no new version publishes until all three succeed.
dimensions.movement_copying: Equal-value reference copies two fields at snapshot time; pin alternative reads its retained version later. Four-pin transfer compares four simultaneous history values, not just the latest pair.
dimensions.destruction: Dropping one pin may reclaim versions no longer selected; non-LIFO release must preserve others. Last shared lease release invokes payload destruction independently of the store.
dimensions.dispatch: Finite scans select visibility and collect slots; read/copy alternatives include their mutex acquisition. Timing cannot extrapolate two-word copying to arbitrary object graphs.
dimensions.concurrency: Pinned reads are repeatable; stronger predicate validation can reject disjoint writes that would violate a joint invariant. RCU would require a separate read-side/grace-period contract and extra retention for escaping snapshots.
dimensions.failure: Fifth active pin refuses unchanged output; stale generations and clock exhaustion refuse. Clone failure leaves existing readers intact; overwritten reused slots must release their old payload.
dimensions.boundary: PostgreSQL isolation passages explain the counterexample but do not certify this finite C store as a database. Pin/copy timing is not a measurement of an RCU implementation.

dimensions.reachable_storage: Sequence counter and two atomic unsigned fields; pointer successor adds a mutex and retained shared payload because the sequence alone cannot keep a pointee live.
dimensions.lifetime: Single writer publishes odd/data/even; a reader accepts only unchanged even sequence. A paused pointer reader retains its node until done, even after replacement and control destruction.
dimensions.mutation_aliasing: All scalar payload accesses remain atomic, including rejected samples. Ordinary racy loads are not repaired by a later validation failure.
dimensions.allocation: Scalar protocol allocates nothing. Pointer replacement stages a shared control before publication and preserves caller ownership on refusal or counter exhaustion.
dimensions.movement_copying: Successful scalar snapshot publishes two copied fields after validation. Failure leaves canaries unchanged; pointer snapshot copies a retained token, not the pointee bytes.
dimensions.destruction: Scalar teardown is quiescent caller discipline. Pointer old-owner destruction waits for the last retained reader and occurs outside the protecting mutex.
dimensions.dispatch: Observed GCC O3 weak reader is loads/comparisons with no hardware fence instruction for the acquire fence; this compiler result does not erase the C ordering obligation.
dimensions.concurrency: One-attempt timing counts successful reads and refusals, comparing a one-try-lock mutex reference. RC11 clients establish only their finite explored executions and edge counterexamples.
dimensions.failure: Zero retry, odd writer, changed sequence and nonwrapping counter retirement refuse without output writes. A writer paused while odd can deny every reader within its bounded attempt budget.
dimensions.boundary: The public C++ proposals are not adopted C17 features. Neither scalar sequence validation nor clean TSan output proves pointer reclamation or arbitrary weak-ISA behavior.

dimensions.reachable_storage: Capacity4 channel plus one callback in flight, worker/control records and retained handle count. Context storage remains separately owned until worker join and final handle release.
dimensions.lifetime: All signals pass through one executor; request/end/cancel state precedes callback dispatch. Cancellation does not release an in-flight callback context.
dimensions.mutation_aliasing: Control mutex serializes demand and terminal state. Callback can request or cancel under the explicit reentrancy rules; recursive delivery is rejected.
dimensions.allocation: Stream control and channel slots are inline. Worker creation may fail without consuming the context; payload is copied unsigned in this adapter, not an implicit deep-cloned object.
dimensions.movement_copying: Accepted input copies one unsigned value. Per-item and batch16 requests deliver exactly the same N ordered values; batching changes request count, not delivery credit accounting.
dimensions.destruction: Close/cancel wakes blocked producers; worker must join and all handles release before context drop. A nonreturning callback prevents quiescence despite a finite buffer.
dimensions.dispatch: Executor calls next/terminal indirectly and never overlaps signals. Per-item request count is N; batch16 count is ceil(N/16), checked independently of timing.
dimensions.concurrency: Several producers use actual pthread exclusion and one executor. Slow-subscriber WAIT/DROP/FAIL policies have different accepted/dropped accounting and cannot be compared as identical delivery guarantees.
dimensions.failure: Zero/maximum demand, terminal-without-credit, late emit and recursive signals are explicit boundaries. FULL/BUSY/CLOSED preserve owners/handles as specified; counts retire without wrap.
dimensions.boundary: Selected Reactive Streams rules guide demand/serialization comparison; unsigned C statuses and fixed capacities are not JVM interoperability or full protocol certification.

findings: Weak push emits mov stores while SC push emits xchg stores.
Weak steal emits a locked stack fence and locked cmpxchg; SC steal uses locked cmpxchg without that separate fence.
Weak sequence reader has no emitted hardware fence instruction; acquire ordering still constrains the compiler.
mfo_start caches backend/context before indirect invocation; msg_complete has no object read following the receiver call.
